news.title: EU Icons for labelling AI-generated content | Shaping Europe's digital future
news.claim: The European Union has introduced a set of standardized icons for deployers of generative AI to label content such as deepfakes and AI-generated text, supporting transparency obligations under the AI Act.
news.why_it_matters: These icons help individuals clearly recognize artificially generated or manipulated content, reducing risks of misinformation and deception as transparency rules become enforceable in August 2026.
evidence_terms: icons are freely available and a integral part of Section 2 of the Code of Practice
The icons have 4 variations: black, white, black with 50% transparency and white with 50% transparency
performance improved across all measures when the basic icon was accompanied by a text label
directly embedded into the deepfake or published text

news.title: Navegar no Regulamento Inteligência Artificial - Shaping Europe's digital future
news.claim: The European Commission updated its comprehensive guidance on navigating the AI Act, clarifying the enforcement framework, governance structures like the AI Office, and compliance timelines for high-risk systems.
news.why_it_matters: Multilingual official guidance is essential for providers and deployers across the EU to navigate the transition to full applicability of the Act, which began on August 2, 2026.
evidence_terms: primeira lei abrangente do mundo para a IA
Regulamento Inteligência Artificial será aplicável dois anos após a entrada em vigor, em 2 de agosto de 2026
Serviço para a IA é responsável por gerir e fazer cumprir as obrigações
abordagem uniforme da IA baseada no risco

daily_topic: Implementation of EU AI Act Transparency and Governance Standards
listener_takeaway: The EU is moving into an active enforcement phase for the AI Act, providing businesses with practical tools like standardized icons for content labelling and updated multilingual guidance to ensure compliance with new transparency requirements.
